help.introEn: A radio conversation of about four minutes on the institution Germans trust more than any other: the Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe. A presenter asks, a constitutional law professor answers: why the court came to Karlsruhe in 1951 and not to Bonn, how its sixteen judges are elected, what a constitutional complaint is and why of five thousand a year only a few dozen succeed, which rulings changed the country, from the census ruling to the climate decision, and whether a court that strikes down laws is not too powerful. In language terms you hear what you practised last. First, adjective formation, from which legal language draws its precision: verfassungswidrig and verfassungsgemäß, grundrechtsrelevant, unabhängig, unanfechtbar, zweidrittelmehrheitlich, höchstrichterlich, karlsruherisch (jokingly), bindend, einstimmig, mehrheitsfähig. Second, proverbs and fixed phrases with which the guest sharpens his answers: Wo kein Kläger, da kein Richter; Vor Gericht und auf hoher See ist man in Gottes Hand; Gleiches Recht für alle; Unrecht Gut gedeihet nicht; Wer die Macht hat, hat das Recht, and what he thinks of it. Several questions test whether you interpret a proverb correctly in context.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: An unconstitutional law is void; the ruling on it is unappealable and binding on all state organs.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The judges are elected by two-thirds majority so that no candidate can command a majority without the opposition.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: -gemäß = in accordance with; -widrig = against; -fähig = capable (verfassungsfähig does not exist).
help.tips[0].en.title: Forming the adjectives of legal language
help.tips[0].en.text: -widrig (against): verfassungswidrig, rechtswidrig, gesetzeswidrig. -gemäß / -konform (in accordance with): verfassungsgemäß, grundgesetzkonform. -relevant: grundrechtsrelevant. -fähig (can): mehrheitsfähig, beschwerdefähig. -bar (can be): anfechtbar, überprüfbar; un-: unanfechtbar, unabhängig, unmittelbar. -lich: höchstrichterlich, gerichtlich, gesetzlich. Participles as adjectives: bindend, geltend, angefochten, verkündet. Numeral + -ig / -lich: einstimmig, zweidrittelmehrheitlich. Whoever knows the building blocks understands a word they have never heard.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: No plaintiff, no judge: Karlsruhe examines no law that nobody challenges, however questionable it may be.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Might makes right, they used to say; the court is the institution meant to refute that sentence every day.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: Both, a trial and a voyage, are out of one's own hands: one can only hope.
help.tips[1].en.title: Proverbs on law and power
help.tips[1].en.text: Wo kein Kläger, da kein Richter: without a complaint nothing is examined; a court does not act on its own. Vor Gericht und auf hoher See ist man in Gottes Hand: the outcome is uncertain. Gleiches Recht für alle: the law applies regardless of the person. Unrecht Gut gedeihet nicht: ill-gotten gains bring no happiness. Wer die Macht hat, hat das Recht: cynical claim that the stronger makes the rules; a state under the rule of law is meant to refute exactly that. Recht haben und Recht bekommen sind zwei Paar Schuhe: being in the right does not automatically mean winning. In listening: a proverb often quotes a position the speaker then contradicts.
help.rememberEn[0]: -widrig (against), -gemäß (in accordance), -fähig (can), un…bar (cannot), -lich, participle: verfassungswidrig, unanfechtbar, bindend.
help.rememberEn[1]: Wo kein Kläger, da kein Richter; vor Gericht und auf hoher See …; Recht haben und Recht bekommen sind zwei Paar Schuhe.
help.examEn: Conversations with an expert about institutions, where you must understand technical vocabulary and figurative phrases, are a typical listening text in the C2 exam.
help.hookEn: Sixteen judges in red robes, five thousand complaints a year, and eighty per cent of Germans trust them. Hear how the court in Karlsruhe works and why it may strike down laws.
